newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Six of Jinro Group affiliates chosen for bailout.
newsitem.headline: Six of Jinro Group affiliates chosen for bailout.

text.p: Six of 24 affiliates of South Korea's Jinro Group have been designated for "normalisation" and will be bailed out, the group's prime creditor, the Commercial Bank of Korea, said on Monday in a statement.
The six firms are Jinro Ltd, Jinro Industries Co, Jinro General Foods Co, Jinro-Coors Brewing Co, Jinro Construction Co and Jinro Mass Merchandising Inc, the statement said.
Jinro Group, the nation's 19th largest conglomerate, has experienced financial troubles because of heavy debts.
The statement said promissory notes owed by the six firms would be frozen from Monday, according to an agreement among the nation's banks and other financial institutions.
Last week the nation's financial institutions set up a committee to help finance cash-short firms.
The statement said the committee would meet on April 28 to discuss Jinro Group affairs.
But it did not mention the fate of the remaining firms.
Jinro said last week it would sell part of its property and affiliates to pay back debts estimated at 3.2 trillion won.
The group also said it would cut the number of its 24 affiliates to around 10 through mergers or sell-offs.
A recent string of corporate failures have hit South Korean financial markets and the economy, already ailing under a widening current account deficit and plunging company earnings.
